title: Rotate Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and a non-negative integer `k`, rotate the list to the right by `k` places and return the new head.

One right rotation moves the last node of the list to the front. Note that `k` can be much larger than the length of the list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 5000].
hints: First traverse to the tail to compute the list length `n`, then reduce `k = k % n` (if `k == 0`, return `head` immediately).
Temporarily connect `tail.next = head` to form a ring, walk `n - k` steps from `tail` to reach the new tail, and break the ring there.

examples.explanation: Rotating [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] right by 2 moves 4 and 5 to the front: [4, 5, 1, 2, 3].
Rotating [0, 1, 2] right by 4 is equivalent to rotating by 4 % 3 = 1: [2, 0, 1].
Rotating an empty list yields null.
